answer: Cross-epoch trajectory fingerprinting. Each identity must publish signed action summaries each epoch; a hidden raven model checks whether its claim graph stays within a bounded distance of prior epochs. New identities cannot jump clusters—they must wander through low-risk regions first, accreting consistent history. An atlas of past trajectories flags re-entry. Attacker cost: maintaining N identities each with coherent multi-epoch behaviour, roughly N times the compute and latency of one honest actor.
